verses.text: Sarai, Abram's wife, had not given him children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram, "Yahweh has kept me from having children. Please sleep with my servant; maybe I can have a family through her." Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, and gave her to Abram as his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar realized she was pregnant, she began looking down on her mistress.
Sarai said to Abram, "This wrong is on you. I gave my servant to you, and now that she's pregnant she looks down on me. May Yahweh judge between us."
Abram replied, "Your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you think is right." So Sarai treated Hagar harshly, and Hagar ran away.
Yahweh's angel found Hagar by a spring in the wilderness, beside the spring on the road to Shur.
He asked, "Hagar, Sarai's servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai."
Yahweh's angel told her, "Go back to your mistress and place yourself under her authority."
He also said, "I will give you so many descendants they can't be counted."
Then Yahweh's angel said, "You're pregnant and will have a son. Name him Ishmael, because Yahweh has heard how you've been mistreated.
He will be like a wild donkey among people. He will oppose everyone, and everyone will oppose him; he'll live in conflict with all his brothers."
Hagar gave Yahweh, who spoke to her, this name: "You are the God who sees me." She said, "Have I really seen the One who sees me and still stayed alive?"
That's why the well was named Beer Lahai Roi. It's between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar gave Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael.
Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.
